intent.text: Demonstrate that a decision whose obligations use ONLY canonical verifier schemes (file-exists, mathc, shell-grep, plus text-scan-/tests-/dune-/scripts-/manual- prefixes) emits zero MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN warnings.

commitment: mathc validate returns parse-ok with no MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN diagnostic when every acceptance.all[*].verifier uses a canonical scheme.

outcomes.statement: All five canonical schemes parse-ok without unknown-scheme warnings.

assumptions.statement: The canonical list documented in decisions/verifier-scheme-convention-2026-11.yaml is authoritative for the duration of this test.
assumptions.consequence_if_false: Authors must migrate to a new scheme family

obligations.claim: Every verifier string in this decision uses a canonical scheme.

counterexample: A canonical-scheme conformance fixture does not carry dialectical content for the kernel-checked rule; the kernel requires counterexample + antithesis for mode >= standard regardless of fixture intent, so this fixture carries documentary content naming the strongest objection considered and rejected.
antithesis: This conformance fixture asserts zero MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN warnings when every acceptance.all[*].verifier uses a canonical scheme. The v3 dialectic antithesis slot is unrelated to that assertion; the author considered and rejected the counter-position that a canonical-list demo need not carry dialectic content because its purpose is a parser/validator diagnostic, not a dialectic test. The kernel requires antithesis for mode >= standard regardless of fixture intent, so the fixture carries a documentary antithesis string naming the position considered and rejected.
